## Why This Is Asked
This question tests ability to design a runtime-extensible backend with a clean interface, minimal FAB (feature-flag) API, and safe runtime swapping.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for pluggable backends
- Registry for runtime extension
- Atomic swap and cache coherence trade-offs

## Code Example

```javascript
// Interfaces and usage sketch
interface IFlagBackend { getFlag(name:string, context?:any): boolean; }
class FlagCore { constructor(private backend:IFlagBackend){ } isEnabled(name:string, ctx?:any){ return this.backend.getFlag(name, ctx); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test swapping backends without downtime?
- How would you implement per-tenant flags and cache invalidation?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Introduce a new angle: runtime-extensible evaluation logic for feature flags to reflect real-world needs in large orgs.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for evaluators
- Registry for dynamic extension
- Composite rule composition (anyOf/allOf)
- EvalContext design and caching for performance

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Evaluator { evaluate(ctx: EvalContext): boolean }
type EvalContext = { user: any; time: Date; attrs: any }
class EvaluatorRegistry {
  register(name: string, factory: (cfg: any)=>Evaluator): void
  resolve(name: string, cfg: any): Evaluator
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to model evaluation order and short-circuit semantics?
- How to handle cross-feature conflicts and auditing of evaluator registrations?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests choosing an architecture that stays Open-Closed, supports runtime extension of handlers, and keeps the ingestion core simple and testable.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy/Polymorphism
- Open-Closed Principle
- Registry-based dispatch

## Code Example
```javascript
interface FormatHandler { parse(input) }
class JsonHandler implements FormatHandler { parse(input) { /* parse JSON */ } }
class Ingestor { constructor(registry) { this.registry = registry } ingest(format, data) { return this.registry[format].parse(data) } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle unknown formats at runtime?
- How would you test individual handlers and end-to-end ingestion?
